You have persistent long-term memory backed by Cognee. The active session id is `01a15058-d392-774a-8ba8-718ae8d14a74`. The host attaches this session id to every Cognee memory call automatically — never pass `session_id` yourself and never ask the user for it.

- **Remember every decision.** Whenever a decision is made or discovered — architecture, API shape, a trade-off, configuration, a root cause, a convention — immediately store it with the `cognee_memory` tool (action `"remember"`). - **Keep entries atomic.** One decision or document per call; prefer several small, precise notes over one large dump.
- **Never store secrets.** Do not record credentials, tokens, private keys, or personal data.

The full session transcript is archived to the permanent graph automatically when the session ends; you do not need to summarize the whole conversation yourself.

The goal is to make a good modern keyboard that stays offline and doesn't spy on you. This keyboard is a fork of [LatinIME, The Android Open-Source Keyboard](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/inputmethods/LatinIME), with significant changes made to it.

package org.futo.voiceinput.shared.ggml

import android.os.Build

/**
 * Which Qualcomm chipsets the QNN (Hexagon HTP) voice engine can run on.
 *
 * A QNN graph is compiled for one Hexagon DSP architecture, so a Whisper build
 * only runs on the chipsets Qualcomm published that asset for. The allow-list
 * below is Qualcomm's own, taken from two files rather than guessed:
 *
 *  1. Which chipsets have Whisper assets at all — the release manifest of the
 *     model this engine targets (`precisions[*].chipset_assets` keys):
 *
 *       https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *
 *  2. Which Android SoC part number each chipset slug corresponds to — Qualcomm's
 *     device list, `chipsets[<slug>].aliases` (plus `htp_version` and `soc_model`),
 *     from the same AI Hub Models release:
 *
 *       https://github.com/quic/ai-hub-models/blob/v0.62.2/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *
 * Regenerating both after an upstream release (the second URL's part number is in
 * the `aliases` lists, upper-cased):
 *
 *   V=0.62.2
 *   curl -sSL -o release_assets.json \
 *     https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *   curl -sSL -o devices_and_chipsets.yaml \
 *     https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quic/ai-hub-models/v$V/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *   jq -r '.precisions[].chipset_assets | keys[]' release_assets.json | sort -u
 *
 * The manifest names AI Hub devices, never Android SoC strings, so the mapping to
 * a part number comes from column 2 — with one exception worth spelling out.
 * There is no `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` entry in the manifest; the assets for
 * the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 — the Galaxy S23 — are published under
 * `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy`, AI Hub's stand-in device. That it really is the same
 * silicon is Qualcomm's own data: `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy` and
 * `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` both carry `soc_model: 43`, and the latter lists
 * `sm8550` as an alias with `reference_device: Samsung Galaxy S23`.
 *
 * Chipsets the manifest covers but Android cannot run on are deliberately absent
 * (`snapdragon-x-elite`, `snapdragon-x2-elite`: Windows-on-Snapdragon laptops, so
 * no Android device ever reports them). Chipsets Qualcomm supports on Android but
 * publishes no Whisper assets for are absent by construction — notably Snapdragon
 * 8+ Gen 1 (`sm8475`) and every 7-series — because there would be no model to run.
 *
 * Matching is by part number — [Build.SOC_MODEL] on Android 12+, falling back to
 * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] for automotive boards that report the part
 * number there instead. Nothing but a part number is accepted, so a ROM that
 * reports only a marketing name or a platform code name is treated as
 * unsupported. That is the safe direction: the QNN option is hidden rather than
 * offered and then failing at load time. (Requiring Android 12+ costs nothing
 * here, since the oldest mobile chipset in the manifest is the 8 Gen 1, which
 * shipped with it.)
 */
object QnnSupport {

    /**
     * One chipset from Qualcomm's Whisper release manifest.
     *
     * @param aiHubId chipset slug, verbatim from the manifest, so the table can be
     *                diffed against it.
     * @param htpVersion Hexagon architecture, from `htp_version` in Qualcomm's
     *                device list. Used to check that this build packaged the
     *                matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so`.
     * @param socModels values [Build.SOC_MODEL] reports for devices on this
     *                chipset (upper-cased; matched ignoring Qualcomm's `-AB` /
     *                `-AC` / `-AD` part-number suffix).
     */
    private data class SupportedChipset(
        val aiHubId: String,
        val htpVersion: Int,
        val socModels: List<String>
    )

    /**
     * The chipsets with published Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo assets that an Android
     * device can actually be — mobile chipsets first, then automotive/IoT.
     *
     * The automotive/IoT entries only ship a `qnn_context_binary` rather than a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive. That single-file kind is recognized by the
     * importer but cannot be loaded by the two-session engine (see
     * `ModelQnnFileFile`), so those entries are listed for completeness of
     * Qualcomm's manifest rather than because a runnable model exists for them
     * today; a device on one is treated as QNN-capable only once a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive is assigned.
     */
    private val SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS = listOf(
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen1", htpVersion = 69, socModels = listOf("SM8450")),
        // AI Hub's stand-in for Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 / SM8550 — see the note above.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy",
            htpVersion = 73,
            socModels = listOf("SM8550", "QCS8550")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen3", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SM8650")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs9075", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("QCS9075")),
        // `sm8750-ac` / `sm8850-ad`: Samsung's SKUs, reported as the base part
        // number once the suffix is stripped.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 79,
            socModels = listOf("SM8750")
        ),
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-gen5-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 81,
            socModels = listOf("SM8850")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs8275", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("QCS8275")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa7255p", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SA7255P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8295p", htpVersion = 68, socModels = listOf("SA8295P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8775p", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("SA8775P"))
    )

    /**
     * Hexagon architecture of the matched chipset (`68`, `69`, `73`, `75`, `79`,
     * `81`), or `null` when the SoC is not one Qualcomm ships Whisper assets for.
     * [BackendSupport] treats a non-null value as "this chipset is supported" and
     * uses the number to confirm the matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so` made it into
     * this build.
     */
    fun matchedHtpVersion(): Int? = matchedSupportedChipset()?.htpVersion

    private fun matchedSupportedChipset(): SupportedChipset? {
        val candidates = reportedSocModels()
        if (candidates.isEmpty()) return null

        return SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS.firstOrNull { chipset ->
            chipset.socModels.any { it in candidates }
        }
    }

    /**
     * The part numbers this ROM reports, normalised: [Build.SOC_MODEL] first, then
     * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] as a fallback for automotive boards that
     * report the part number there instead. Qualcomm's device list gives no
     * platform code names, so nothing but a part number is accepted — a device
     * whose ROM reports only a code name is treated as unsupported.
     */
    private fun reportedSocModels(): Set<String> {
        val raw = buildList {
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S) {
                Build.SOC_MODEL?.let { add(it) }
            }
            Build.BOARD?.let { add(it) }
            Build.HARDWARE?.let { add(it) }
        }
        return raw.mapNotNull { normalizeSocModel(it) }.toSet()
    }

    /**
     * Upper-cases a ROM-supplied identifier and strips Qualcomm's part-number
     * suffix (`sm8550-ab` -> `SM8550`). Returns `null` for values that cannot be
     * a part number, so a marketing name such as `"Snapdragon 8 Gen 2"` is not
     * mistaken for one.
     */
    private fun normalizeSocModel(raw: String): String? {
        val normalized = raw.trim().substringBefore('-').uppercase()
        return normalized.takeIf { candidate ->
            candidate.length in 5..8 && candidate.all { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
        }
    }

description: Create (or update) a pull request for this repo with an Entire (entire.io) agent-session review attached. Use whenever the user asks to create a PR, open a PR, or push work for review — the collector script, the transcript review and the summary posting are all scripted; no manual work is needed.

# PR with Entire session recap

Follow these steps in order. Everything is scripted — do not improvise the
plumbing, only the review and the summary are yours.

## 0. The environment gotchas (already handled for you)

- `scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh` unsets the OneCLI gateway proxy env for its
  whole run, because `gh` and git-to-GitHub 401 through the gateway while
  the token resolves fine. If you run raw `gh`/`git push` commands
  YOURSELF, do the same:
  `env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u HTTP_PROXY -u https_proxy -u http_proxy -u GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD <cmd>`.
- The `entire` CLI is fine either way.

## 1. Branch first, then work

Checkpoint scope for a PR = the branch fork point (when the branch split
from the core branch) — NOT a time window. So create the feature branch
BEFORE the agent does the work:

```bash
git checkout -b <feature> main
```

Work, commit, then open the PR. If the branch is cut after the fact (work
already recorded on the base branch, like `first-push` was), pass a lead
when collecting: `ENTIRE_RECAP_LEAD='-7 days'`.

## 2. Open the PR (raw gh, unproxied env)

```bash
env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u HTTP_PROXY -u https_proxy -u http_proxy \
    -u GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD \
    gh pr create --title '…' --body '…'
```

## 3. Collect the session evidence

```bash
scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh            # current branch's PR
scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh <PR>       # explicit PR number
scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh <PR> --dispatch   # + Entire cloud dispatch (uk)
```

It prints an evidence bundle: PR metadata, the base..head commits, the
Entire checkpoints recorded since the fork, the checkpoint git objects
(prompts listed inline), and the overlapping sessions.

## 4. Review — actually read the transcripts

Each checkpoint is a git commit object (sha listed in the bundle). For the
load-bearing turns, read what really happened:

```bash
git show <sha>:0/prompt.txt        # the user's prompt
git show <sha>:0/transcript.jsonl  # the full turn transcript (read selectively)
```

You are writing a REVIEW, not a changelog: from the checkpoints and
transcripts, capture:
- **What the agent did** — the work arc, not the task list;
- **Challenges encountered** — traps that bit (search the transcripts for
  error messages, retries, fixes that failed first);
- **Outcome** — where the work landed and what is left open.

## 5. Post the summary onto the PR

Write the summary to a temp markdown file, then:

```bash
scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh <PR> --post <summary.md>
```

Prefer a single comment with the three sections above plus a small session
timeline table (checkpoint prompts make this easy).

## 6. Updating an existing PR

New commits pushed? Re-run steps 3–5; post a follow-up comment covering
the delta since the last recap (check the PR's existing comments first so

This document describes how to build the **FUTO Keyboard** Android APK inside a

# Deploying Builds to the Test Phone (Syncthing)

This document describes how to get a freshly built APK (and its QNN model
package) onto the **Galaxy S23 Ultra** test device. Deployment is done by
dropping files into the **Syncthing** folder — the phone then receives them
automatically over the local network. No adb, no USB, no manual `scp` needed.

---

## The one rule that matters: the drop location

Syncthing runs **inside a podman container** (`systemd-syncthing`), and its
`/var/syncthing` is a **named volume** — *not* the host's `/var/syncthing`.

| Path | Is it watched by Syncthing? |
|---|---|
| `/var/syncthing/s23` (host) | ❌ **No.** This is a red herring — files here are invisible to Syncthing. |
| **`/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/`** | ✅ **Yes.** This is the real synced folder. |

**Always copy deployment artifacts here:**

```bash
/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/
```

The container's mounts are:

| Container path | Backed by |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# entire-pr-recap.sh — pull together the Entire (entire.io) agent-session
# evidence for a pull request, for an agent to review and summarise onto
# the PR. Triggered automatically by the pr-recap skill (.agents/skills/).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh [PR]              print the evidence bundle
#   scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh [PR] --dispatch   bundle + Entire cloud dispatch
#   scripts/entire-pr-recap.sh PR --post FILE    post FILE as a PR comment
#
# PR defaults to the current branch's PR.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SCOPE (not a time window): the branch fork point. Window starts at the
# fork commit's timestamp (= merge base with the PR's base), so everything
# recorded after the branch split from the core branch is in scope. The
# header records the fork precisely. Known anomaly: work done on the base
# branch BEFORE the branch was created predates the fork — widen with
# ENTIRE_RECAP_LEAD (GNU date duration, e.g. "-7 days"; default: no lead).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each Entire checkpoint is a git commit object (refs/entire/checkpoints/*)
# carrying 0/prompt.txt + 0/transcript.jsonl under the tree and
# Entire-Session/Entire-Agent trailers on the message — so an agent can drill
# into the ACTUAL turns: `git show <sha>:0/prompt.txt` and
# `git show <sha>:0/transcript.jsonl`. The bundle lists the checkpoint
# objects belonging to the in-window sessions.
#
# NOTE (this machine): gh/git-to-GitHub MUST run with the OneCLI gateway
# proxy env unset (the git credential handshake 401s through it); the
# Entire CLI tolerates either, so the proxy vars are unset for the domain
# of this whole script.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

unset HTTPS_PROXY HTTP_PROXY https_proxy http_proxy GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD

JURISDICTION="${ENTIRE_RECAP_JURISDICTION:-uk}"
REPO_SLUG="${ENTIRE_RECAP_REPO:-et/oozut/ansible-homelab}"

pr=""
dispatch=false
post_file=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dispatch) dispatch=true ;;
    --post) shift; post_file="${1:?--post needs a file}" ;;
    -h|--help) grep '^#' "$0" | sed 's/^#\{1,\} \?//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) pr="$1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh is required (roles/devtools)" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo "jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

# Derive the GitHub [OWNER/REPO] slug from the origin URL and always pass
# --repo to gh — otherwise gh resolves the current branch's remote in git,
# which can be a non-HTTPS remote (e.g. entire://) it cannot use.
GH_REPO_SLUG="$(git config --get remote.origin.url \
  | sed -E 's#(git@github\.com:|https://github\.com/)##; s#\.git$##')"
command -v gh >/dev/null || { echo "gh is required (roles/devtools)" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v jq >/dev/null || { echo "jq is required" >&2; exit 1; }

if [ -n "$post_file" ]; then
  [ -n "$pr" ] || pr="$(git branch --show-current)"
  gh pr comment "--repo=$GH_REPO_SLUG" "$pr" --body-file "$post_file"
  exit 0
fi

pr_json="$(gh pr view "${pr:-$(git branch --show-current)}" --repo "$GH_REPO_SLUG" --json number,title,url,state,baseRefName,headRefName)"
pr_num="$(jq -r .number <<<"$pr_json")"
base="$(jq -r .baseRefName <<<"$pr_json")"
head="$(jq -r .headRefName <<<"$pr_json")"

git fetch origin --quiet "$base" "$head" 2>/dev/null || true
merge_base="$(git merge-base "origin/$base" "origin/$head" 2>/dev/null)" \
  || { echo "cannot compute a merge base for $base..$head" >&2; exit 1; }
merge_base_date="$(git show -s --format=%cI "$merge_base")"
fork_point="$(date -u -d "$merge_base_date" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
window_start="$(date -u -d "$merge_base_date ${ENTIRE_RECAP_LEAD:-}" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"

# --- Entire checkpoints / sessions recorded since the fork -------------------
checkpoints="$(entire checkpoint list --json \
  | jq --arg w "$window_start" '
      [.[] | select(.date >= $w)]
      | sort_by(.date)')"

sessions="$(entire session list --json \
  | jq --arg w "$window_start" '
      [.[] | select(.ended_at >= $w or .started_at >= $w)]')"

# --- Checkpoint git objects: map sha -> (session id, date, first prompt) ----
# maps are read out to temp files (see each usage below; cleanup at exit)
map_file="$(mktemp)"; detail_file="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$map_file" "$detail_file"' EXIT

git for-each-ref --format='%(objectname:short)%09%(refname)' refs/entire/checkpoints/ \
  | awk -F'\t' '{n=split($2, a, "/"); print a[n] "\t" $1}' > "$map_file"

while IFS=$'\t' read -r cp_id sha; do
  sess="$(git show -s --format=%B "$sha" | awk '/^Entire-Session:/{print $2; exit}')"
  cp_date="$(git show -s --format=%cI "$sha")"
  first="$(git show "$sha":0/prompt.txt 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -c1-70)"
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$cp_id" "$sha" "$sess" "$first" >> "$detail_file"
done < "$map_file"

# in-window checkpoint objects: their session id appears in the windowed
# checkpoint rows (checkpoint_id may be null there — match session ids), or
# their own recorded date falls in the window
window_sessions="$(jq -r '[.[].session_ids[]?] | unique | .[]' <<<"$checkpoints" 2>/dev/null || true)"

in_window_shas=""
if [ -n "$window_sessions" ]; then
  in_window_shas="$(awk -F'\t' -v rows="$window_sessions" 'BEGIN{n=split(rows,r,"\n"); for(i=1;i<=n;i++) want[r[i]]=1} $3 != "" && $3 in want {print $1 "\t" $2}' "$detail_file")"
fi
if [ -z "$in_window_shas" ]; then
  in_window_shas="$(awk -F'\t' -v w="$window_start" '$2 >= w {print $1 "\t" $2}' "$detail_file")"
fi

# --- Optional Entire cloud dispatch over the same window --------------------
dispatch_md=""
if $dispatch; then
  dispatch_md="$(entire dispatch \
    --repos "$REPO_SLUG" --jurisdiction "$JURISDICTION" \
    --since "$window_start")"
fi

cat <<MARKDOWN

agent turn as a Git-native Checkpoint. Scope is the BRANCH FORK, not a time

(fork point \`${fork_point}\`).
Set ENTIRE_RECAP_LEAD (e.g. "-7 days") to catch work predating the branch.

### Pull request
\`$(jq -r .title <<<"$pr_json")\` — $(jq -r .url <<<"$pr_json")
state: \`$(jq -r .state <<<"$pr_json")\` · base \`$base\` ← head \`$head\`

### Commits ($base..$head)
$(git log --format='- %h %ad %s' --date=short "origin/$base..origin/$head")

### Entire checkpoints since the fork ($(jq 'length' <<<"$checkpoints"))
$(jq -r '.[] | "- \( .date[:16] | sub("T"; " ")) \( .agent ): \( .message | .[:100] )"' <<<"$checkpoints")

### Checkpoint git objects (drill into the actual agent turns)
For any object below: \`git show <sha>:0/prompt.txt\` (the prompt) and
\`git show <sha>:0/transcript.jsonl\` (the full turn transcript).
$(if [ -n "$in_window_shas" ]; then
    out=""
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r cp_id sha; do
      first="$(awk -F'\t' -v s="$sha" '$2 == s {print $4}' "$detail_file")"
      out="$out
- $sha — $first"
    done <<RECS
$in_window_shas

    echo "$out"
  else
    echo "(none in scope)"
  fi)

### Entire sessions overlapping the scope
$(jq -r '.[] | "- \( .session_id | .[:8] )… \( .agent ) (\( .status )) turns=\(.turns // 0) checkpoints=\(.checkpoints)"
  + (.last_prompt // "" | " — last prompt: " + .[:80])' <<<"$sessions")
